arabic_blocks: [1140] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن مخرمة بن سليمان عن كريب مولى ابن عباس أنه أخبره عن عبد الله بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه بات عند ميمونة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها وهي خالته قال: فاضطجعت على عرض الوسادة واضطجع رسول الله ﷺ وأهله في طولها فنام رسول الله ﷺ حتى انتصف الليل أو قبله بقليل أو بعده بقليل ثم استيقظ رسول الله ﷺ فجلس فمسح النوم عن وجهه بيده ثم قرأ العشر آيات خواتيم سورة آل عمران ثم قام إلى شن معلقة فتوضأ منها فأحسن وضوءه ثم قام يصلي قال عبد الله بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما فقمت فصنعت مثل ما صنع ثم ذهبت فقمت إلى جنبه فوضع رسول الله ﷺ يده اليمنى على رأسي وأخذ بأذني اليمنى يفتلها بيده فصلى ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم أوتر ثم اضطجع حتى جاءه المؤذن فقام فصلى ركعتين خفيفتين ثم خرج فصلى الصبح
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik informed us, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, the mawla of Ibn ‘Abbas, that he informed him, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He spent the night with Maymunah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who was his maternal aunt. He said: I lay down across the pillow, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until midnight, or a little before it, or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, awoke, sat up and wiped the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the ten verses at the end of Surat Al ‘Imran. Then he went to a hanging worn waterskin and performed ablution from it, performing his ablution well. Then he stood to pray.

‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said: I got up and did as he had done. Then I went and stood beside him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed his right hand on my head and took my right ear, twisting it with his hand. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two light rak‘ahs, then went out and prayed the morning prayer.

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us. ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from his father, from Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to reconcile Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf, and the time for prayer came. Bilal came to Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, and said, “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has been delayed. Will you lead the people?” He said, “Yes, if you wish.” Bilal called the iqamah for prayer. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, went forward and prayed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came walking through the rows, making his way through them, until he stood in the first row. The people began clapping.
Sahl said: Do you know what tasfih is? It is tasfiq—clapping.

Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, did not turn around during his prayer. When they increased it, he turned, and there was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the row. He signalled to him, “Stay where you are.” Abu Bakr raised his hands and praised Allah. Then he stepped backwards behind him, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and prayed.

We used to say the greeting in prayer and name people, and some of us would greet others. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard it and said:

english_blocks: Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. Yunus said: Al-Zuhri said: Anas ibn Malik informed me:

While the Muslims were at the Fajr prayer on Monday and Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was leading them in prayer, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, suddenly appeared to them, having drawn aside the curtain of ‘A’ishah’s room, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. He looked at them as they stood in rows and smiled, laughing. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, stepped backwards, thinking that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to come out to the prayer. The Muslims were on the point of being distracted in their prayer out of joy at the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when they saw him. He signalled with his hand that they should complete it. Then he entered the room and let down the curtain. He died that day.

english_blocks: And al-Layth said: Ja‘far related to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

A woman called to her son while he was in a hermitage. She said, “O Jurayj!” He said, “O Allah, my mother and my prayer!” She said, “O Jurayj!” He said, “O Allah, my mother and my prayer!” She said, “O Jurayj!” He said, “O Allah, my mother and my prayer!” She said, “O Allah, may Jurayj not die until he looks upon the faces of prostitutes.”

A shepherdess who tended sheep used to come to his hermitage. She gave birth, and she was asked, “By whom is this child?” She said, “By Jurayj.” He came down from his hermitage. Jurayj said, “Where is this woman who claims that her child is mine?” He said, “O baby, who is your father?” He said, “The shepherd.”

english_blocks: Mahmud related to us. Shababah related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

He performed a prayer and said: “Satan appeared to me and rushed at me to interrupt my prayer. Allah gave me power over him, and I choked him. I had intended to tie him to a pillar until morning came upon you and you could look at him. Then I remembered the words of Sulayman, peace be upon him: ‘My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me.’ So Allah sent him back humiliated.”

english_blocks: Adam related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. Al-Azraq ibn Qays related to us. He said:

Shu‘bah said: He was Abu Barzah al-Aslami.
A man of the Khawarij began saying, “O Allah, do something to this old man!” When the old man finished, he said:

I heard what you said. I went on six expeditions or seven expeditions or eight with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and witnessed his making things easy. english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah. He said: ‘A’ishah said:

The sun was eclipsed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and recited a long surah. Then he bowed and prolonged it. Then he raised his head, then began another surah. Then he bowed when he had completed it, and prostrated. Then he did that in the second. Then he said:

They are two signs among the signs of Allah. When you see that, pray until it is relieved for you. In this place where I stood, I saw everything I was promised. I even saw myself wanting to take a bunch from Paradise when you saw me beginning to move forward. And I saw Hell, its parts crushing one another, when you saw me move back. I saw in it ‘Amr ibn Luhayy, who was the one who set the sawa’ib loose.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent me on an errand for him. I went, then returned after completing it. I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not reply to me. Something came into my heart which Allah knows best. Then I greeted him, and he replied to me. He said, “What prevented me from replying to you was that I was praying.” He was on his riding animal, facing a direction other than the qiblah.

english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us. ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

It reached the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that something had happened among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf at Quba. He went out with some of his companions to reconcile them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delayed, and the time for prayer came. Bilal came to Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, and said, “O Abu Bakr, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has been delayed, and the time for prayer has come. Would you lead the people?” He said, “Yes, if you wish.” Bilal called the iqamah for prayer. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, went forward and pronounced the takbir for the people. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came walking through the rows, making his way through them, until he stood in the row. The people began clapping.
Sahl said: Tasfih is tasfiq—clapping.

He said: Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, did not turn around during his prayer. When the people increased it, he turned, and there was the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He signalled to him, directing him to pray. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, raised his hand and praised Allah. Then he stepped backwards behind him until he stood in the row. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and prayed for the people. When he finished, he turned towards the people and said, “O people, why, when something happened to you in prayer, did you begin clapping? Clapping is only for women. Whoever has something happen to him in his prayer should say, ‘Glory be to Allah.’”

Then he turned to Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and said, “O Abu Bakr, what prevented you from praying for the people when I signalled to you?” Abu Bakr said, “It was not fitting for the son of Abu Quhafah to pray in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

arabic_blocks: [1163] حدثنا إسحاق بن منصور حدثنا روح حدثنا عمر هو ابن سعيد قال: أخبرني ابن أبي مليكة عن عقبة بن الحارث رضى الله تعالى عنه قال صليت مع النبي ﷺ العصر فلما سلم قام سريعا دخل على بعض نسائه ثم خرج ورأى ما في وجوه القوم من تعجبهم لسرعته، فقال: ذكرت وأنا في الصلاة تبرا عندنا فكرهت أن يمسي أو يبيت عندنا فأمرت بقسمته
english_blocks: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us. Rawh related to us. ‘Umar—he is Ibn Sa‘id—related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, from ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

I prayed ‘Asr with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he gave the greeting of peace, he got up quickly and went in to some of his wives. Then he came out and saw on the people’s faces their astonishment at his haste. He said, “While I was in prayer, I remembered some uncoined gold with us. I disliked its remaining with us until evening or overnight, so I ordered that it be distributed.”

arabic_blocks: [1164] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير حدثنا الليث عن جعفر عن الأعرج قال: قال أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال رسول الله ﷺ: إذا إذن بالصلاة أدبر الشيطان له ضراط حتى لا يسمع التأذين فإذا سكت المؤذن أقبل فإذا ثوب أدبر فإذا سكت أقبل فلا يزال بالمرء يقول له اذكر ما لم يكن يذكر حتى لا يدري كم صلى قال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن إذا فعل أحدكم ذلك فليسجد سجدتين وهو قاعد وسمعه أبو سلمة من أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. Al-Layth related to us, from Ja‘far, from al-A‘raj. He said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away, passing wind so that he does not hear the call. When the caller to prayer falls silent, he comes back. When the iqamah is called, he turns away. When he falls silent, he comes back. He keeps telling the person to remember things he had not been remembering, until he does not know how much he has prayed.
Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: If one of you does that, let him prostrate twice while seated.
Abu Salamah heard it from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b informed me, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi. He said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said:

He recited such-and-such a surah.”
